name: Learning with strategic or adversarial elements
gist: Analyzing how learning algorithms perform when facing adversarial actors, noisy conditions, or game-theoretic interactions where agents have competing goals.
explain: A spam filter learns to block emails that look like spam. Spammers, knowing this, modify their emails to evade detection. The filter learns again, adapting to new spam tactics. This cycle continues: the learner and the adversary are both adapting, trying to outmaneuver each other. In game theory, two chess players study each other's strategies, each assuming the opponent is optimal. In mechanism design, a platform must set rules knowing that users will strategically respond to those rules. This subtheme examines learning in adversarial and strategic settings: how do you learn when the environment or an opponent is actively working against you?

The difficulty is that in adversarial settings, the standard assumptions of learning theory break down. You assume training data reflects the environment you will encounter, but an adversary deliberately sends data designed to fool your model. You cannot simply retrain when the adversary adapts because you must decide quickly. In game-theoretic scenarios, you must reason about what the opponent will do, but the opponent is reasoning about what you will do, leading to circular predictions. The learner also faces a tradeoff: should you commit to a predictable strategy (which an opponent can exploit) or use randomness (which is less efficient but harder to exploit)? Finding stable strategies where no player wants to deviate requires different tools than standard learning.

Researchers study adversarial reliability — training models that maintain good performance even when inputs are slightly perturbed by an attacker, so the model does not fail catastrophically. They analyze reliable algorithms that work even in the worst case (rather than the average case), providing guarantees that an adversary cannot break by exploiting worst-case scenarios. They study no-regret learning — algorithms where cumulative performance degrades gracefully as the environment changes or an adversary attacks, such that the algorithm did not have a much better strategy in hindsight, which guarantees that even faced with an optimal opponent, the algorithm accumulates reward at a reasonable rate over time because no single strategy could do vastly better. They examine game-theoretic learning where multiple agents simultaneously learn strategies, analyzing convergence to equilibria — stable outcomes where no agent can do better by unilaterally changing strategy, which is important because such stability means learning stops and decisions can be relied upon. They also tackle strategic classification, where data points (people or systems) may misrepresent themselves to influence the model's decision. In all cases, the goal is learning algorithms that remain effective against clever, intentional opposition.

papers.title: Adversarially Pretrained Transformers may be Universally Robust In-Context Learners
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that adversarially pretrained transformers can provide free adversarial robustness to downstream tasks despite expensive initial training.

papers.title: Anytime Detection of Strategic Deviations in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Provides statistically sound online monitoring of equilibrium departure for normal-form and stochastic games with finite-time detection guarantees.

papers.title: Bandit Learning in Matching Markets Robust to Adversarial Corruptions
papers.contribution: Both algorithms provide theoretical guarantees with upper bounds on optimal stable regret and lower bounds demonstrating optimality.

papers.title: Revisiting the Bertrand Paradox via Equilibrium Analysis of No-regret Learners
papers.contribution: They demonstrate that no-external-regret learners can converge to high-price outcomes while stronger guarantees like no-swap regret shape more competitive low-price behavior, supported by theoretical analysis and experiments.

papers.title: The Value Function Semi-Algebraic Set in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes
papers.contribution: Reveals that partial observability induces fundamentally nonlinear constraints producing richer geometric structure with isolated local maximizers dependent on initial state distribution.

papers.title: Theory of Continual Learning Against Data Poisoning Attacks
papers.contribution: The framework proves no defense succeeds against linear-proportion task poisoning, but identifies defensible regimes and provides verified convergence guarantees for robust defense.

papers.title: Transformers as Measure-Theoretic Associative Memory: A Statistical Perspective and Minimax Optimality
papers.contribution: Establishes matching minimax lower bounds proving convergence optimality, providing theoretical grounding for Transformer generalization on long distributional contexts.

papers.title: When Flatness Does (Not) Guarantee Adversarial Robustness
papers.contribution: Prove loss must curve sharply away from data manifold for global robustness, revealing that adversarial examples lie in large flat regions where models are confidently wrong.

papers.title: A Noise Sensitivity Exponent Controls Large Statistical-to-Computational Gaps in Single- and Multi-Index Models
papers.contribution: Establishes that NSE controls the onset of computational bottlenecks in high-noise single-index models and statistical-computational gaps in specialization transitions of multi-index models.

papers.title: Black-Box Assisted Regression: Phase Transitions and Minimax Optimality
papers.contribution: Provides finite-sample minimax characterization with phase transition at δc(n)≈n^(-β/(2β+d)), showing the estimator matches leading minimax risk up to an additive validation-selection cost.

papers.title: Computing Equilibrium beyond Unilateral Deviation
papers.contribution: Proves fixed-parameter lower bounds on computational complexity and presents algorithm matching those bounds.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Causal Abstractions
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees for both empirical and Gaussian environments, enabling principled selection of ambiguity-set radii and establishing quantitative guarantees on worst-case abstraction error, with empirical robustness to environmental shifts and m

papers.title: Feature compression is the root cause of adversarial fragility in neural networks
papers.contribution: Theoretical analysis explains adversarial fragility through feature compression; predictions match experiments on practical networks including ImageNet models.

papers.title: Improved Distribution Estimation in $\ell_\infty$
papers.contribution: Resolves open questions from Kontorovich & Painsky (2025) regarding ℓ∞ distribution estimation; provides both theoretical bounds and empirical validation.

papers.title: Learning a Game by Paying the Agents
papers.contribution: The principal can learn utility functions to any desired precision using a polynomial number of rounds and can then steer agents to desired equilibria.

papers.title: Mitigating Spurious Correlation via Distributionally Robust Learning with Hierarchical Ambiguity Sets
papers.contribution: The method demonstrates strong robustness on minority group shifts where existing methods fail, while achieving superior performance on standard benchmarks.

papers.title: Noise Tolerance of Distributionally Robust Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive performance with order of magnitude reduction in computational cost on physical PDE benchmarks and electric grid data.

papers.title: On the Existence of Consistent Adversarial Attacks in High-Dimensional Linear Classification
papers.contribution: The theory reveals that vulnerability to label-preserving perturbations grows with overparameterization, offering theoretical insight into model sensitivity mechanisms.

papers.title: On the Sharp Input-Output Analysis of Nonlinear Systems under Adversarial Attacks
papers.contribution: Provides sharp input-output analysis and proves optimality by constructing matching lower bounds for nonlinear systems under probabilistic adversarial attacks.

papers.title: Optimal Rates for Feasible Payoff Set Estimation in Games
papers.contribution: First minimax-optimal rates established for set-valued payoff inference, enabling downstream applications in counterfactual analysis and mechanism design.

papers.title: Quantifying the noise sensitivity of the Wasserstein metric for images
papers.contribution: Establish theoretical basis for benefits of Wasserstein metrics over Euclidean distance in noisy settings, supported by cryo-electron microscopy case study.

papers.title: Random Spiking Neural Networks are Stable and Spectrally Simple
papers.contribution: Shows that wide LIF-SNN classifiers are stable on average due to concentration of Fourier spectrum on low-frequency components, with experiments confirming stability properties persist in trained networks.

papers.title: Robust Linear Dueling Bandits with Post-serving Context under Unknown Delays and Adversarial Corruptions
papers.contribution: Achieves delay-regime-agnostic regret bound of O(d(sqrt(T) + C + D)) with nearly matching lower bounds up to sqrt(d) factor for adversarial delays.

papers.title: Strategic Candidacy in Generative AI Arenas
papers.contribution: Proves YRWR is approximately clone-robust and improves ranking accuracy under producer honesty, with simulations calibrated to Chatbot Arena data.

papers.title: Trapped by simplicity: When Transformers fail to learn from noisy features
papers.contribution: Transformers succeed at noise-robust learning of k-sparse parity and majority functions but fail on random k-juntas, revealing fundamental learning limitations.
